These are estimates from my own prior knowledge of NAS-Bench-201, not computed from the benchmark data.

The main priors I used:
- Setting an edge to none hurts more when the remaining paths are few, so it is worse when a parent edge is none (the edit has a LOWER effect there, since fewer alternative paths remain). A none edit also hurts less when an alternative path exists.
- Conv ops on the edge adding the most to accuracy matter more when other edges are weak or absent.
- Interactions are often small or inconsistent across the three datasets, so most claims get low probabilities.
